highlights.title: Revelio Labs: Monopsony in the US Labor Market — Is Worker Power Back?
highlights.summary: US workers now retain ~80 cents of each marginal dollar earned, up from ~70 cents pre-2022, with variation by industry, union status, and AI exposure — providing a direct wage-share signal linked to AI adoption.

highlights.title: Beyond the Laggard Myth: Time-Series Analysis of AI Job Market Dynamics in Construction
highlights.summary: One of the first cross-industry time-series analyses of AI job postings in construction, benchmarking AI hiring growth against digital and traditional sectors to challenge linear diffusion assumptions.

highlights.title: NY Fed Liberty Street Economics: Evaluating New LinkedIn Labor Market Tightness Indicators
highlights.summary: The NY Fed evaluates LinkedIn-derived labor market tightness measures as real-time alternatives to JOLTS, providing new high-frequency job-seeker-to-opening ratios with implications for wage pressure forecasts.

highlights.title: NBER: Saving for the Machines — Task Models, Capital Accumulation, and Automation Growth
highlights.summary: In a standard task model, capital supply governs the magnitude of automation-driven growth; the paper argues task-structure shifts alter returns to machine accumulation, with implications for labor's share as automation expands.

highlights.title: NBER: Public R&D and the Automation of Manufacturing — Evidence from the Space Race
highlights.summary: Space Race–era public R&D measurably shifted US manufacturing toward automation, providing historical causal evidence that government-funded technology investment accelerates physical-task displacement.

highlights.title: The Global AI Divide: Cross-National Analysis of AI Integration and Labor Market Inequality
highlights.summary: Cross-national analysis finds AI adoption generates productivity gains while intensifying structural labor-market inequalities, with differential impacts across income groups and geographies.

highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: US Labor Market Snapshot — October 2026
highlights.summary: Monthly snapshot covering US job postings, wages, unemployment, and openings as of October 2026, flagging current directional trends across key labor-market indicators.

highlights.title: What is Work For? Labor, Politics, and Meaning in the Age of AI — Cross-National Survey
highlights.summary: Original survey of 8,234 working-age adults across UK, US, Denmark, and India quantifies non-monetary motivations for work and attitudes toward AI-driven job change, with cross-national breakdowns.

themes: Wage-share recovery and monopsony easing as AI adoption accelerates across industries
Historical and theoretical models deepening understanding of automation's displacement and capital-accumulation dynamics
High-frequency alternative labor-market indicators (LinkedIn, Indeed) gaining institutional validation alongside lagging official series
